name: LUCA

VINIT.justification: The unorganized state of organic monomers before the emergence of biological order.

TANCH.justification: The closed metabolic boundary that maintains the internal environment against external equilibrium.

AFWD.justification: The forward synthesis of complex macromolecules from simpler precursors.

AREV.justification: The breakdown of polymers into monomers which facilitates recycling and error correction.

CLINK.justification: The sequential chaining of enzymatic reactions where the product of one serves as the substrate for the next.

IMSCRIB.justification: A system of molecules where each member is produced by at least one reaction catalyzed by another member of the same set.

FSPLIT.justification: The division of a single progenitor cell into two distinct but genetically identical daughter cells.

FFUSE.justification: The recombination of genetic material from distinct lineages back into a single functional genome.

EVALT.justification: The successful transmission of genetic information and metabolic stability to the next generation.

EVALF.justification: A failure in replication or metabolism that leads to the cessation of the biological process.

ENGAGR.justification: A state where RNA functions simultaneously as both genetic information carrier and catalytic enzyme.

IFIX.justification: The permanent and irreversible fixation of the codon-to-amino-acid mapping shared by all extant life.

phase_3.void_description: Abiotic environment lacking self-replicating informational polymers
phase_3.true_description: Metabolically active state with successful protein synthesis
phase_3.both_description: The protocell stage where internal and external chemistry are not yet fully distinct

steps.domain_action: The emergence of organic precursors in a hydrothermal vent environment
The synthesis of long-chain fatty acids and nucleotides
The formation of self-assembling lipid vesicles that encapsulate chemistry
The coupling of thioester metabolism to early phosphate-based energy transfer
The coexistence of ribozymes performing both template and catalyst roles
The divergence of metabolic strategies into distinct chemical gradients
The selection of the most efficient ATP-synthase precursor
The collapse of unstable protocell membranes
The integration of successful metabolic modules into a single proto-organism
The fixation of the 20 standard amino acids into the translation machinery
The transition from RNA to DNA for stable long-term information storage
The establishment of the ribosome as the central self-referential translator
The final closure of the LUCA genome as the common ancestor for all subsequent life

phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Cell cycle regulation and enzymatic kinetics
phase_5.alfs_store: The conserved core of the 16S ribosomal RNA

phase_6.cycle_cost: ATP hydrolysis to ADP and inorganic phosphate
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: High-energy chemical gradients at the vent-ocean interface
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Low-energy waste products and increased local cellular order
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system exports entropy to the environment to maintain internal negentropy
